text.text: Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr. will miss El Clasico against FC Barcelona on Oct. 25 after being suspended for four games for the red card he received in Real Madrid's last home game, against Villarreal at the Bernabeu. The Brazilian forward came on in the 52nd minute and was sent off 20 minutes later. Vinicius Jr. thought he had scored, and Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho celebrated alongside his team and ran over to him a few seconds before VAR ruled out the goal and sent him off. The VAR check showed Vinicius Jr. had pulled Nathan Saliba's hair before scoring. The Spanish Football Federation's rules state that pulling an opponent's hair is violent conduct, and Vinicius was suspended for the upcoming four Real Madrid matches against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. The federation's competition committee gave Vinicius a two-game ban for "violent conduct, without the possibility of playing the ball" and two additional games "for arguing with the referee with an aggressive attitude and having to be restrained by his teammates." text.text: The Indian ODI skipper, Shubman Gill, won the ICC Player of the Month award on Tuesday. This is the fifth time he has won the prestigious award. Gill was recognised for his brilliant performances against the West Indies in September. He finished ahead of compatriot Abhishek Sharma and Zimbabwe’s Sikandar Raza.The record for the most ICC Player of the Month awards previously belonged to Pakistan’s Babar Azam, who had won it three times. Babar claimed the honour on three occasions between April 2021 and August 2023. The Indian ODI and Test skipper went past Babar after his Test exploits against England in July 2025. Gill’s latest accolade puts him level with women’s cricketer Hayley Matthews, who has also won it five times. He previously won it in January and September 2023, and then again in February and July 2025. For the uninitiated, the award considers players' performances across all formats.Gill prevailed against strong competitionIndia’s blazing T20I opener, Abhishek Sharma, posed a formidable challenge to Gill. The left-handed batter was in imperious form during the series against Afghanistan. In the first match, he scored 82 off 32 balls, then 39 off 19 in the second.

text.text: Red Bull have confirmed that Laurent Mekies will continue his role as Team Principal through 2031. Laurent Mekies has signed a long-term contract extension to remain as Red Bull's CEO and Team Principal, lasting through the 2031 season. The French engineer was promoted from Racing Bulls in July 2025 and led the Milton Keynes-based outfit through a challenging start to this year, which saw them drop behind their rivals under the new regulations. However, their consistent work over the course of 2026 – guided by Mekies – finally paid off as Max Verstappen secured back-to-back victories in Malaysia and Singapore, bringing Red Bull back into contention for regular wins. text.text: Max Verstappen will share a track with Valentino Rossi for the first time in a competitive setting this weekend, with the pair set to go wheel-to-wheel at the GT World Challenge Endurance finale in Portimão. Verstappen lines up in a Mercedes AMG GT3 EVO, while Rossi will be behind the wheel of a BMW M4 GT3 EVO. The four-time F1 drivers' champion has already made clear he would rather not run into the MotoGP legend out on circuit. But is there really anything for Verstappen to worry about? Few people are better placed to answer that than Kelvin van der Linde. The South African BMW factory driver spent a lengthy spell as Rossi's team-mate and has shared a car with the Italian on several occasions, giving him a unique insight into how the nine-time MotoGP champion has adapted to four wheels. Speaking to RacingNews365 earlier this year, Van der Linde gave a frank assessment of where Rossi stands as a GT racer. "It's a tricky question," he says. text.text: McLaren 's Andrea Stella confirmed that the team is "not finished" with its Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri talks, after the pair collided in Singapore. Both MCL40s were sent into synchronised spins when the drivers made contact late in the Sprint around Marina Bay. McLaren is happy to move on from analysing blame in the incident, but wants to achieve a clear, united plan moving forward. The papaya duo, in battle for P6, collided on the final lap of the Singapore Sprint. Both cars went spinning, with Norris only able to get going again. He finished P8. Quick to apologise to the team, the Brit had initially defended his right to go for the gap. After the Grand Prix on Sunday, he shifted that stance to admit the move should never have been attempted at all. Piastri noted his teammate's apology and said they had moved on. Norris even offered to help his younger teammate, who was chasing Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari, in the closing stages of the Grand Prix. It was a welcome sight for team principal Stella, who confirmed that conversations remain ongoing within the Woking squad. text.text: Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen have explained what happened at the start of Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix, where the Ferrari driver had the best launch but failed to outdo his rival. Despite starting from the dirty side of the track – which admittedly wasn’t as dirty as usual given it had rained the day before – Leclerc had his front axle nearly alongside Verstappen’s within seconds. The four-time world champion, however, drove his opponent towards the inside, to the extent that Leclerc’s front wheels briefly exceeded the white line. The Monegasque braked earlier, and Verstappen was able to retain the lead from the outside. “You don't have much time to think in those moments,” Leclerc said. “I just saw that Max had a bit of a difficult start. I had quite a good start, so I went alongside him. Then there wasn't much space anymore, but I would have done exactly the same. “Then it's quite tricky. I was on the left, a little bit behind him, couldn't see the panels on the right, so you lose a little bit all your references because that's normally on the right that you have your references to brake. The Six Kings Slam has been postponed. Riyadh Season announced on Tuesday that the third edition of its exhibition event, originally scheduled for October 21, 22 and 24, will instead be held from December 27 to 30, 2026. The reason given in the announcement is organizational, though Tennis Majors understands the postponement is linked to the international situation. “The decision reflects Riyadh Season’s commitment to delivering sporting events to the highest standards, following an assessment of the organizational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and their potential impact on the quality of the audience experience,” the release reads. text.text: Cristiano Ronaldo has shown his connection to Saudi Arabia with a gesture that carried added significance after a tense night in Riyadh. The Portuguese forward waved a scarf featuring the Saudi flag following Al-Nassr's 3-1 victory over FC Neftchi Fergana in the AFC Champions League Elite, reaffirming his bond with the country and its fans who welcomed him when his career was under scrutiny. There has also been speculation that he could end his playing career in Saudi Arabia. The match was delayed by an hour after an aerial missile alert and explosions were reported across the city. Yemen-based Houthi rebels launched ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, while Saudi-led coalition forces intercepted and destroyed the incoming projectiles. The fixture went ahead once authorities confirmed the danger had passed. Ronaldo scored Al-Nassr's second goal in the 42nd minute, taking his career tally to 981 goals during the match in Riyadh. Despite the security concerns surrounding the fixture, Al-Nassr maintained their composure to secure a 3-1 win and claim three points in the continental competition. report.text: The AFC Champions League Elite match between Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr and Uzbekistan's Neftchi Fergana was delayed by an hour after Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense issued a security alert. The match, which took place in Riyadh's Al-Awwal Park, had a sparse crowd who waited in their seats as the players waited for kick off. The Saudi-led coalition said it had twice intercepted and destroyed ballistic missiles launched Monday by the Houthi rebels toward Riyadh. At least three explosions could be heard Monday night in the city. Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense, which had warned residents through alerts sent to their phones, later said the danger had passed. Ultimately, Al-Nassr won the match 3-1 with Angelo Gabriel and Ronaldo scoring in the first half. Alisher Odilov pulled a goal back for the visitors before a 78th minute own goal sealed the Saudi team's win. The Iran-backed Houthis have claimed a series of recent missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport that killed at least 13 people and wounded over 300 over the weekend. report.text: Before this weekend, Max Verstappen had not won a race in Singapore Red Bull's Max Verstappen took his second dominant victory within a week as he secured his first win in the Singapore Grand Prix. Verstappen fought off an attack from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc off the start line to control the race from start to finish. The win followed his and Red Bull's maiden victory of the year in Malaysia last weekend and sprint race success in Singapore on Saturday, confirming the team's re-emergence as a major force. Leclerc took second as team-mate Lewis Hamilton finished sixth after a baffling strategy that was a consequence of the Briton choosing not to pit when asked. Hamilton, trying to last out on a set of soft tyres for a mammoth 44 laps, lost out in the closing laps to Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. Antonelli's third place combined with team-mate George Russell finishing only ninth after starting from 19th extends the Italian's championship lead to 102 points. report.text: Zizou Bergs recorded the biggest win of his career after stunning Carlos Alcaraz in straight sets at the Shanghai Masters. The Belgian world No.39 held his nerve throughout a tightly contested encounter to prevail 7-5, 7-6(4) after more than two hours on court. Bergs is the second player this year to beat Alcaraz while ranked outside the top 20, after Sebastian Korda at the Miami Masters. He is also the lowest-ranked player to beat the Spaniard since his fellow countryman, David Goffin, did so last season. “It's a level of disbelief and not feeling too much,” Bergs said of his shock win. “We're now one minute after a match, so it's tough to calm down but I'm very happy.” Coming into the match having won just two out of his 16 meetings against top 10 players, Bergs gave it his all against the world No.3 and refused to be disheartened when losing a break advantage in both sets. Overall, he won 79% of his first service points and produced 24 winners. “I just felt like last week in Tokyo, I really was in good shape, ” Bergs said of his form. “I'm very happy with how I handled the tiebreak. report.text: Austin Reaves exposed the Golden State Warriors defense last night while helping the Los Angeles Lakers build a 20-point third-quarter lead. That the Warriors came back to win 101-89 feels less important than Golden State's biggest preseason issue, which has been point-of-attack defense. (Note: Turning the ball over is a close second.) Let's go over how the Lakers exposed the Warriors' poor on-ball defense before addressing what they can do to fix it from a personnel perspective. In 25 minutes, Reaves had 28 points on 10-of-18 shooting with seven assists and seven turnovers. The Warriors deserve credit for swarming him into a high-turnover game, but the bigger-picture issue is how often they gave up easy drives, especially considering Reaves was the only major threat with Luka Doncic resting. The first defensive mistake came from Curry. Any time you're in a ball-screen situation at the point-of-attack defender, the first rule is to be ready if the offensive player rejects the screen. report.text: On a night dominated by the apparent status of Kristaps Porzingis, the absence of the Latvian big was felt at times during the Golden State Warriors’ 101-89 win over the Los Angeles Lakers at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. Steve Kerr’s intention to spread the floor in a so-called ‘5-out’ alignment banked on players who are able to space to floor — including their center. Porzingis happens to fit that profile, while also being 7-foot-3-inches. Without Porzingis — and also not having Al Horford available tonight — the Warriors were not only small, they were bereft of shooting and spacing personnel. That was apparent at times during this game, where the Warriors were able to rally back from a significant deficit, albeit during a time when both teams’ main characters’ nights were finished (one of them, Luka Doncic, did not suit up for the Lakers). Once again, it was rookie Yaxel Lendeborg who stood out. He finished with 17 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists in just under 24 minutes of time on the floor.
